assessments.reasoning: The pinned Microsoft TOP reference at lines 63–67 limits WITH TIES to SELECT with ORDER BY and explicitly illustrates an integer limit of five producing seven rows when two additional rows match the boundary ORDER BY values.

challenge.method: Compared the five-to-seven example with the PERCENT section, the product syntax block and the no-tie outcome. Checked a composite sort order and the same-commit SET ROWCOUNT exception to distinguish a possible overflow from an unconditional cardinality guarantee.
challenge.results: The integer case shows overflow for matching boundary sort keys. A row sharing only one component of a different multi-column ordering key does not meet the illustrated full-key tie. The article leaves the order within ties arbitrary, and a session-level row cap can affect results. The existential can-return-more claim survives these cases.

limitations: Interpret a tie as a match on the full ORDER BY key. The finding is confined to SQL Server SELECT and the possibility of exceeding the count with boundary ties.
